minutes.headline: Committee voted to return pre-K and grades 6-12 to full in-person on April 5 and approved the FY22 budget.
minutes.summary: After a short public hearing with no public questions, the committee approved the FY22 school budget at a 2.5 percent increase, with grant-funded positions and three offset reductions. It then voted a full return to school for pre-K and grades 6-12 on April 5, following a long superintendent presentation on state mandates, distancing, buses, lunch space, cleaning, vaccination and survey data. Line item transfers, the personnel report, the 2021-22 calendar, the FY21 budget update and an air quality report were also handled, then the committee went into executive session.

public_comment.topic: Educators' concerns about the state's return timeline, staff not yet vaccinated, and learning of the district's grade 6-12 plans through a parent email; asked the committee to give educators time.
Second public comment period; no one spoke.

budget_items.topic: Grant-funded positions (SR2 and special ed grants)
budget_items.what_was_said: Third social worker, math specialist, paraprofessionals and tech support funded through the SR2 grant; part-time psychologist through the special ed grant.
Estimated cost for the rest of the year; state funding for pooled testing ends April 18.
DESE funds pooled testing until then, after which districts would bear the cost.
Districts not complying with the return mandate could lose Chapter 70 funding.
Any surplus would go to facilities and grounds, PPE purchases, technology and shifting salaries from revolving accounts; the local budget will not be exceeded.
Two small negative accounts remain: primary school secretarial overtime and district journal supplies.

decisions.decision: Administration will begin posting and interviewing for FY22 budgeted and grant-funded positions now, but not appoint or award contracts until after Town Meeting.
Superintendent will analyze structured learning hours and may return recommending the May early release days be changed to full days.
Superintendent to update the committee at coming meetings on staff drop-in sessions and union discussions about the full return.
Committee will break at seven o'clock for the posted budget hearing and then resume the agenda.
Bus seating limited to two per seat; new transportation requests go on a wait list prioritized by distance (two miles, then a mile and a half, then closer).

what_happened.line: The committee voted 5-0 to return pre-K and grades 6-12 to full in-person learning on April 5.
The committee approved the FY22 school budget as presented, 5-0, after closing a public hearing at which no one asked questions.
The recommended budget is an overall 2.5 percent increase; a health insurance premium holiday freed money to fit grant-funded positions within it.
Bus seating is limited to two per seat, and new transportation requests go on a wait list ranked by distance from school.
The committee accepted the 2021-22 calendar and the FY21 budget update, both 5-0, and approved several line item transfers.

why_it_matters: The FY22 school budget approved here is the figure that goes to Town Meeting, where residents vote on the town's share of school spending.
The full return changes busing, building use and testing costs for families, and state pooled testing funding is shown ending April 18, after which districts would bear that cost.
Some FY22 positions rest on grants (SR2 and special education) rather than the general fund, so their cost to the town budget depends on what happens when those grants end.
watch_next: Town Meeting, after which administration may appoint staff and award contracts for FY22 positions.
Superintendent updates on staff and union discussions about the full return, and on whether the May early release days become full days.
